mainEntity.name: What is the R-value, and why is it important for insulation?

acceptedAnswer.text: R-value measures an insulation material's resistance to heat flow. A higher R-value indicates greater insulating power and better thermal performance. The appropriate R-value for your home depends on your climate zone and the specific area being insulated (e.g., attic, walls). For instance, attics generally require higher R-values than walls. Choosing the correct R-value ensures optimal energy efficiency, comfort, and compliance with local building codes, leading to lower energy bills and a more comfortable indoor environment.
acceptedAnswer.description: R-value indicates insulation's heat flow resistance; higher R-values mean better thermal performance. It's crucial for energy efficiency and compliance with climate zone recommendations.
